findings.description: Evaluating V2 freezes caller-owned VX contract objects through evidence output.
Malformed structures throw generic exceptions; unrecognized replay enums are admitted into a complete economic reading. Cyclic/BigInt consumed metadata also escape governed failure.
An explicit FRED sourceId is overwritten as VIX_OFFICIAL by the normalizer; row-level conflicting provenance is ignored.
R0 calendars and rows with future capturedAt are accepted; R2 rows with UNKNOWN replay class are admitted.
Assembly drops row availability/status/replay and third-contract lineage, and uses lexical maximum for offset-bearing timestamps. Late or R2 parents can become eligible R0 evidence.
Futures field is ignored and duplicate history identities silently select the first; reversing the supplied catalog changes a valid reading into INCOMPLETE.
TICKERS, GROUPS and INITIAL_OPTIONALS are mutable exports. Mutation of TICKERS crashes subsequent evaluation.
Invalid previous duration with censored=false produces an uncensored duration of two sessions.
The streak loop rescans the full packet and slices the calendar once per session: O(n²) on a long same-sign history. This is a bounded-loop implementation defect, with no need for broader tuning.

One unit wiring assertion compares evaluateRegime pillars to its own evaluateCore dependency. It is self-confirming for methodology and is excluded from independent acceptance evidence. The 464 frozen golden expected values and 1930 Python expected rows are independent of TS.
Declared Next 16.3.1 and installed 16.2.7 differ before Sweeper; manifest and lock are among the 819 byte-preserved pre-Builder files.
18 existing warnings occur outside Builder files; compare exact diagnostic tuples again in final verification.

probe_adjudication: Initial cycle/BigInt probes attached unsupported values to ignored root keys; ignored extra keys are not a defect. v2 places them inside consumed packet metadata and records actual generic exceptions. Original initial log retained.
